thread:
jen: heads up — AcmeCorp on Dedicated (pool id rp-49f7) is getting intermittent 429s and some 401s during their nightly ingestion burst. Customer says latency also spikes to 800-1200ms. They expect their SLA 95th p95 < 200ms for reserved tier.

acme-infra: confirmed — pattern at 02:00-02:15 UTC, QPS jumps from ~180 to ~900 for ~10 min. We saw both x-ratelimit and x-auth failures. Attaching minimal repro steps below.

jen: repro steps please. need quick triage and whether this is config drift, rate-limit gating, or auth token expiry. Customer is on a dedicated reserved pool with commit 4k rps? Their contract says reserved throughput 1,000 rps sustained, burst to 5k allowed for short windows.

acme-infra: steps we ran:
1) curl to generate load: `for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done`
2) during burst we observe responses:
- ~12% return 429 with headers: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 12`
- ~1% return 401 with body `{"error":"invalid_token"}` (token rotation service logs show no failures)
- p95 latency climbs to 1.1s

acme-infra: also posted server-side log excerpt: `req_id=tx-99 pool=rp-49f7 qps=920 token_bucket=0.00 allowed=false -> 429`

kai: thanks — initial theory: reserved pool token-bucket is getting exhausted because our throttle config uses a short smoothing window (10s) and a conservative burst_capacity. If customer expects burst to 5k for 10 min, our bucket/BW settings probably don't match contract. Also 401s could be a side-effect: overloaded auth cache -> failing introspection -> transient 401s.

tom: pulled pool config:
```
reserved_pool_id: rp-49f7
sustained_qps: 1000
burst_capacity_tokens: 3000
smoothing_window_sec: 10
auth_cache_ttl_sec: 60
```
This config yields effective instantaneous cap ~4000 (sustained + burst) but with 10s smoothing, long 10-min bursts will deplete bucket.

sri: ops notes — customer committed to reserved throughput 1k sustained, but contract also allows short bursts of 5k for spikes <= 2 minutes. We should not permit 10-minute unthrottled 5k bursts unless they purchased additional burst credits.

jen: acme says their SIEM/ingest job is a 10-minute window, they assumed "burst" covers it. So mismatch between contract language and customer expectations. We need to: 1) provide immediate mitigation to reduce 429s and auth failures, 2) give clear next steps and config guidance, 3) propose a plan for long-term alignment (billing/contract or config changes).

kai: mitigation options (fast):
- Temporarily increase burst_capacity_tokens to 12000 for rp-49f7 (rollout via console -> will increase short-term cost exposure but buy breathing room).
- Smooth bursts using request shaping at customer side (client-side leaky bucket) to keep effective ingress <= 2500 rps.
- Increase auth_cache_ttl to 300s to reduce token introspection pressure.

jen: can we do the temporary config change now? and capture telemetry so we can demonstrate impact?

sri: I can apply a temporary safe ramp: set burst_capacity_tokens=12000 and smoothing_window_sec=30 for the next 3 hours, monitor. I'll also enable higher auth cache for the pool.

support-bot: automation notice — change request submitted: change_id=chg-20240315-0815, applied by sri, rolling to nodes in pool rp-49f7.

acme-infra: confirming — after config change we see 429s drop to <1%, p95 back to ~210-260ms, auth 401s gone. Thanks. Want to discuss longer-term: either amend contract to allow 10-min bursts or customer throttles job.

kai: long-term recommendations:
- Align SLA/contract wording and reserved pool enforcement: either add a burst_credit bucket in billing that accrues and can be spent on multi-minute bursts, or enforce strict per-minute caps that match contract.
- Provide an API to request temporary burst increase with automated billing flags (self-serve).
- Improve server-side metrics: expose token_bucket_balance and smoothing_window in the console so customers can self-diagnose.

jen: i'll draft a support response summarizing the repro, root cause (bucket exhaustion + auth cache pressure), immediate mitigation (temporary burst and smoothing increase), and options for long-term (contract/billing add-on or client-side shaping). Also include recommended observability queries:
```
# prometheus-ish
sum(rate(redwood_request_count{pool="rp-49f7",status="429"}[1m])) by (instance)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="rp-49f7"}[5m])) by (le))
redwood_pool_token_bucket_balance{pool="rp-49f7"}
redwood_auth_cache_misses_total{pool="rp-49f7"}
```

jen: anyone object to me sending that to Acme and proposing a 3-month trial of a burst-credit addon?

kai: go ahead. I'll follow up with an internal RFC on burst-credit design and dev task to expose token_bucket_balance in Console.

tom: i'll schedule a post-mortem with infra and account team to update runbooks and contract language.

jen: great — thanks all. closing loop once Acme accepts the next steps. :thumbsup:
